title: EGA III.7.7.9: representing modules, relative ampleness and removing presentations
review_boundary: Primary-only mathematical comparison of the French clauses and the actual Stacks statements/proofs. No subagents, printed-page collation, proof-assistant validation or independent-review claim.
source_read_boundary: Pinned diplomatic transcription; the conclusion below concerns its explicit wording, not a claim of collated original-print errata.

rows.hypotheses_and_scope: Formation of the coherent representing modules Q, R and N in III.7.7.6-7.7.8 commutes with arbitrary base change, with the original two-term presentation retained in the N case.
derivation: Work on an affine open of Y, then an affine open of Y' mapping into it. For the coherent base-flat sheaf F, the perfect direct image has a finite-projective model E^0 -> E^1 -> ... in nonnegative degrees. Q=coker((E^1)^vee -> (E^0)^vee) represents H^0 with arbitrary module coefficients.

After A -> B, EXCHANGE identifies the new direct image with E tensor_A B. Finite-projective duals commute with base change and tensor preserves cokernels, so the new representing module is Q tensor_A B. This argument concerns the representing cokernel; it does not assume arbitrary pullback commutes with sheaf Hom of nonprojective modules.
For the kernel of two section functors, R=coker(Q' -> Q). The induced map is preserved by the natural base-change identifications; right exactness of tensor gives R_B.

For N, the right-exact presentation E_1 -> E_0 -> G -> 0 remains right exact after any pullback. The pulled-back E_j remain finite locally free, and their duals commute with pullback. Reduce to the preceding R case. Gluing uses unique isomorphisms compatible with the representing natural transformations.

rows.hypotheses_and_scope: A coherent G has a two-term finite-vector-bundle presentation over the inverse image of every affine base open when an f-ample line bundle exists. The transcription's literal unrestricted global-presentation claim does not follow and is false in general.
derivation: Over an affine base open V, X_V is Noetherian and quasi-compact, and the relative ample line bundle is ample in the absolute sense. AMPLEQUOT gives a finite direct sum of negative powers surjecting onto G|X_V. Its kernel is coherent, so repeat the same argument to obtain E_1 -> E_0 -> G|X_V -> 0.

This is global on X_V, and is global on X when Y itself is affine. It also follows globally if X has the resolution property, for example if X carries an absolute ample line bundle. It does not justify gluing these vector bundles to one presentation on all of X.

For the unrestricted global reading, use Y formed by gluing two affine planes along the complement of their origins, as in DOUBLED with n=2. It is Noetherian and quasi-separated. Its two affine chart intersection is not affine, so the diagonal is not affine. DIAGONAL implies Y has no resolution property; on a Noetherian scheme this means some coherent sheaf is not a quotient of any finite locally free sheaf.

Set X=Y and f=id_Y, which is proper. O_Y is f-ample because its restriction to each affine base open is ample there. The literal global statement would give every coherent sheaf a finite-vector-bundle quotient, contradicting the preceding result. The useful relative/local assertion remains valid.

rows.hypotheses_and_scope: For proper f over locally Noetherian Y, coherent base-flat F and arbitrary coherent G, the functor M -> f_*Hom_X(G,F tensor f^*M) is represented by Hom_Y(N,M) for a coherent N, without a global two-term vector-bundle presentation of G.
derivation: Over an affine base Spec A, apply EXTMODEL(A) with E=G[0], the target complex F[0], and m=0. It gives one perfect K with H^i(K tensor_A^L M)=Ext_X^i(G,F tensor_A M) for every A-module M and every i<=0. The negative Ext groups vanish, so K has nonnegative Tor amplitude; its upper Tor bound is finite because K is perfect.

PERFECT gives a finite-projective representative E^0 -> E^1 -> ... with no negative terms. Put N=coker((E^1)^vee -> (E^0)^vee). Then Hom_A(N,M)=ker(E^0 tensor M -> E^1 tensor M)=Hom_X(G,F tensor_A M) naturally for every M.

The proof of EXTMODEL constructs K using a perfect approximation P -> G that is an isomorphism on H^0 and has no positive cohomology. This is not a claim of a global vector-bundle resolution of G. The same distinction is explicit in HOMPROOF.

For a principal open of the affine base, apply the natural formula to localized coefficient modules M_s. On X, finite presentation of G makes sheaf Hom commute with this scalar localization. On the quasi-compact quasi-separated X, global sections of quasi-coherent modules commute with this filtered localization. Thus the natural module formula restricts to the sheaf formula.

On overlaps, both locally constructed coherent modules represent the same localized functor. Yoneda gives unique compatible isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle condition; the modules glue on Y, including when Y is nonseparated. Taking global sections gives the global Hom formulation. No extra resolution-property or projectivity hypothesis is imposed.

limitations: Only the three clauses of III.7.7.9 are covered; the preceding 32-row comparison is a separate checkpoint.

The global reading of the relative-ampleness clause is refuted using existing Stacks results. The affine-local form is valid. No original-print collation or historical-source errata admission is claimed.
